title: The Gracchi Brothers
objective: After this level you can explain the land reforms of the Gracchi and why they ended in violence.
summary: As estates swallowed small farms, the tribunes Tiberius and Gaius Gracchus pushed land and grain reforms. Both were killed.

cards.headline: Two brothers tried to give land to the poor. Both were killed for it.
cards.body: Rome’s rich were getting richer while its small farmers lost their land. Two brothers tried to fix that, and found out what fixing it would cost.

cards.headline: Rich estates, poor farmers
cards.body: Picture your family farm next to a giant estate worked by enslaved people. By the 2nd century BCE, wealthy Romans had built huge estates like that, while many small farmers lost their land. In 133 BCE a tribune named Tiberius Gracchus proposed an answer: give public land to poor citizens. Remember Level 16? Tribunes of the plebs were elected to protect ordinary Romans. This one took the job literally.

cards.headline: Politics turns deadly
cards.body: The argument didn’t end with a vote. A mob of senators and their supporters killed Tiberius, the first great outbreak of political bloodshed in Rome in centuries. His brother Gaius picked up the cause and pushed even wider reforms, including cheap grain for citizens. In 121 BCE, Gaius was killed too. Two brothers, two reform plans, two funerals.

cards.fact: After the Gracchi, Roman political fights could be settled with violence.
cards.context: That was the real turning point. Not the land, but the lesson: if you couldn’t win the argument, you could get rid of the person making it. Disputes that used to be settled by votes could now be settled by violence. Watch for that lesson in the levels ahead. Rome learned it far too well.

mascot.line: Keep this one. Much of the Republic’s remaining story is this lesson, learned again.

cards.headline: The Gracchi: remembered
learned: Estates grew as small farmers lost land
Tiberius Gracchus proposed land reform in 133 BCE

questions.prompt: Put the story of the Gracchi in order, from first to last.
items: Give public land to poor citizens
questions.explanation: In 133 BCE Tiberius proposed to give public land to poor citizens, and a mob killed him. His brother Gaius picked up the cause, and in 121 BCE Gaius was killed too.

questions.prompt: Why were the deaths of the Gracchi a turning point?

options.label: Political disputes were now settled by violence
They ended the long Conflict of the Orders for good
They gave the poor all public land

questions.explanation: Killing sitting reformers showed that votes and vetoes could be overruled by force.

questions.prompt: Tiberius Gracchus held which Roman office, meant to protect plebeians?

options.label: Consul, one of two yearly leaders
Censor, keeper of the citizen rolls

questions.explanation: Both brothers were tribunes of the plebs, the office created to protect ordinary citizens.
